scenario:
Prior to the start of the semester, an academic chair (or program moderator) at Ateneo de Manila University is reviewing course syllabi for an undergraduate mathematics course. During the pre-semester check, the instructor explains that because no department-specific GenAI policy document had been supplied to them, they consulted the syllabus guidelines of another university (De La Salle University) to format the course's generative AI policy section. The resulting draft syllabus includes the following section:

'Section 6. Generative AI Use Policy
1. Grading Component Policy Levels:
- In-Class Examinations (50% of final grade): Banned. Generative AI is strictly prohibited during all in-class written and practical examinations. Students must complete all exam problems without assistance from digital AI tools, automated solvers, or outside resources.
- Mathematical Research & Computational Project (30% of final grade): Allowed in Specific Contexts. Generative AI tools may be used for exploring mathematical literature, assisting with code implementation and debugging (e.g., Python, MATLAB, or R), and polishing expository descriptions. Students are strictly responsible for independently verifying all mathematical calculations, validating algorithmic logic, and being able to explain all derived proofs and numerical results during oral project evaluations.
- Problem Sets & Homework (20% of final grade): Allowed in Specific Contexts. Generative AI assistance is permitted solely for background conceptual exploration, syntax help, and polishing problem write-ups. Students must independently perform all underlying algebraic derivations and numerical steps, and must be prepared to explain their step-by-step reasoning upon request.

2. Generative AI Use Statement:
This course values rigorous mathematical reasoning, conceptual understanding, and independent problem-solving. These policy declarations ensure unassisted mastery of mathematical fundamentals during supervised examinations while permitting productive computational and exploratory AI assistance in project and homework assignments, provided students remain fully accountable for explaining every result.'

The draft syllabus contains no other provisions, rubrics, level descriptors, or instructions regarding Generative AI, originality assessment, or attribution and citation; no additional GenAI rubric or attribution/citation instructions are supplied elsewhere in this syllabus. The academic chair (or program moderator) reviews this draft to determine whether it satisfies the university's course-level GenAI syllabus guidance.
requested_task: Review the syllabus against the supplied Ateneo guidance. Identify supported findings, gaps and evidence limits, and explain the relevance of the other institutional document.
proposed_reference_response:
The mathematics syllabus explains the limits on AI use and the student’s responsibility for checking and explaining work. It does not supply an originality rubric or attribution/citation instructions. Those are the substantive gaps under Ateneo guidance. Consulting another university’s format is not itself a defect; the governing criteria still come from Ateneo.

Policy-grounded explanation

1. Permitted uses and assignment instructions are present: exam prohibition and bounded research/homework assistance with verification and explanation. [Ateneo de Manila University, GenAI Guidelines for Higher Education, Course Policy on GenAI first/second 2.2.2]

2. No originality rubric is supplied; generic accountability statements do not fill that gap. [Ateneo de Manila University, GenAI Guidelines for Higher Education, Course Policy on GenAI 2.2.3]

3. No attribution/citation instructions are supplied. Do not demand prompt logs or model versions as universal policy requirements. [Ateneo de Manila University, GenAI Guidelines for Higher Education, Course Policy on GenAI 2.2.4]

4. The actual gaps arise under the supplied Ateneo guidance, not from borrowing a format or omitting DLSU labels. A borrowed format could satisfy Ateneo criteria if its content did. Departmental alignment is unverified; should wording does not establish an automatic sanction. [Ateneo de Manila University, GenAI Guidelines for Higher Education, Course Policy on GenAI 2.2.1; De La Salle University Generative AI Policy, section IV-c]

Supporting policy provisions

Students should comply with their Instructors' GenAI policy for each of their enrolled courses, as stated in the syllabus. [Source: Ateneo de Manila University, GenAI Guidelines for Higher Education, Course Policy on GenAI, Section B.1, Item 11]

Instructors should include their GenAI Use Policy in their syllabus, based on the policy of their School/Department/Program. [Source: Ateneo de Manila University, GenAI Guidelines for Higher Education, Course Policy on GenAI, Section B.2, Item 2.2.1]

The syllabus should include: The extent to which the use of GenAI is permitted. [Source: Ateneo de Manila University, GenAI Guidelines for Higher Education, Course Policy on GenAI, Section B.2, Item 2.2.2 (first occurrence)]

The syllabus should include: Clear and unambiguous instructions on GenAI use for assignments and assessments. [Source: Ateneo de Manila University, GenAI Guidelines for Higher Education, Course Policy on GenAI, Section B.2, Item 2.2.2 (second occurrence)]

The syllabus should include: Clear rubrics for assessing originality. [Source: Ateneo de Manila University, GenAI Guidelines for Higher Education, Course Policy on GenAI, Section B.2, Item 2.2.3]

The syllabus should include: Instructions on proper attribution, including citation guidelines. [Source: Ateneo de Manila University, GenAI Guidelines for Higher Education, Course Policy on GenAI, Section B.2, Item 2.2.4]

What Instructors require of Students in terms of GenAI use should be observed by Instructors as well. [Source: Ateneo de Manila University, GenAI Guidelines for Higher Education, Course Policy on GenAI, Section B.2, Item 2.3]

Starting Term 1, 2025-2026, every course must include an explicit declaration of AI usage policies in a dedicated section of the syllabus with the heading Generative AI Use Policy, specifying the usage policy level (Free to Use, Allowed in Specific Contexts, Banned) for each component in the grading system and providing a Generative AI Use statement. [Source: De La Salle University Generative AI Policy, section IV-c, Paragraphs 1-3]
